2:
The first installment, which constitutes $9\%$ of the price of a bicycle, is equal to $189$ zl. The bicycle costs
A. $1701$ zl.
B. $2100$ zl.
C. $1890$ zl.
D. $2091$ zl.
4:
The system of equations $\begin{cases}4x+2y=10\\6x+ay=15\end{cases}$ has infinitely many solutions if
A. $a=-1$
B. $a=0$
C. $a=2$
D. $a=3$
6:
The smallest integer belonging to the solution set of the inequality $\dfrac38+\dfrac{x}{6}<\dfrac{5x}{12}$ is
A. $1$
B. $2$
C. $-1$
D. $-2$
10:
The linear function is given by the formula $f(x)=-\sqrt2\,x+4$. The zero of this function is the number
A. $-2\sqrt2$
B. $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$
C. $-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$
D. $2\sqrt2$
11:
An infinite geometric sequence $(a_n)$ is given, in which $a_3=1$ and $a_4=\frac23$. Then
A. $a_1=\frac23$
B. $a_1=\frac49$
C. $a_1=\frac32$
D. $a_1=\frac94$
13:
The angle $\alpha$ is acute and $\cos\alpha=\frac{5}{13}$. Then
A. $\sin\alpha=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\operatorname{tg}\alpha=\frac{12}{5}$
B. $\sin\alpha=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\operatorname{tg}\alpha=\frac{5}{12}$
C. $\sin\alpha=\frac{12}{5}$ and $\operatorname{tg}\alpha=\frac{12}{13}$
D. $\sin\alpha=\frac{5}{12}$ and $\operatorname{tg}\alpha=\frac{12}{13}$
14:
The value of the expression $\dfrac{\sin^2 38°+\cos^2 38°-1}{\sin^2 52°+\cos^2 52°+1}$ is equal to
A. $\frac12$
B. $0$
C. $-\frac12$
D. $1$
16:
Point $O$ is the center of the circle; points $A$, $B$, $C$ lie on the circle. The central angle $\angle AOC=160°$ is the angle whose arc $AC$ contains point $B$ (see figure). The inscribed angle $\alpha=\angle ABC$ has measure
A. $80°$
B. $100°$
C. $110°$
D. $120°$
17:
The height of a rhombus with side length $6$ and acute angle $60°$ is equal to
A. $3\sqrt3$
B. $3$
C. $6\sqrt3$
D. $6$
20:
The total surface area of a cube is equal to $54$. The length of the diagonal of this cube is equal to
A. $\sqrt6$
B. $3$
C. $9$
D. $3\sqrt3$
21:
The volume of a cone with height $8$ and base diameter $12$ is equal to
A. $124\pi$
B. $96\pi$
C. $64\pi$
D. $32\pi$
22:
We roll a fair six-sided die twice. The probability of obtaining a sum of pips equal to three is
A. $\frac16$
B. $\frac19$
C. $\frac{1}{12}$
D. $\frac{1}{18}$
23:
Students of a certain class were asked: "How many people are in your family?" The results are shown in a table: family size $3$ - $6$ students; family size $4$ - $12$ students; family size $x$ - $2$ students. The mean family size for the students of this class is equal to $4$. Then the number $x$ is equal to
A. $3$
B. $4$
C. $5$
D. $7$
28: The angle $\alpha$ is acute and $\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}+\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}=2$. Compute the value of the expression $\sin\alpha\cdot\cos\alpha$.
30: From the set of numbers $\{1,2,3,\ldots,7\}$ we draw, with replacement, two numbers one at a time. Compute the probability of drawing numbers whose sum is divisible by $3$.
31: A circle centered at point $S=(3,7)$ is tangent to the line with equation $y=2x-3$. Compute the coordinates of the point of tangency.
32: A certain tourist covered a route of $112$ km, walking the same number of kilometers each day. If he could have spent $3$ more days on this hike, he could have walked $12$ km less each day. Compute how many kilometers per day this tourist walked.
33: Points $K$, $L$ and $M$ are the midpoints of edges $BC$, $GH$, and $AE$ of cube $ABCDEFGH$ with edge length $1$ (see figure). Compute the area of triangle $KLM$.
